rejected_model_findings.title: Headline 10.5% ROI rests on OM rent of AED 3.31m, above the rent roll and with no costs deducted

evidence.reason: OCR page: quote matches text 0.97 but the figure '84' is not in the OCR text ('Excellent ROI 10.5% | 64 units | Ready & tenanted')

rejected_model_findings.why: The OM gives a yearly rent of AED 3,310,000 and an unqualified 'ROI' of 10.5% against the AED 31.5m asking price. The 10.5% is consistent with 3.31m divided by 31.5m, so it looks like a gross figure that deducts no operating costs. The rent roll (as of 2026-10-31) shows in-place rent of AED 3,010,500, which is also its potential rent. That is about AED 300k a year below the OM figure. On that rent the gross yield is about 9.6% before any expenses. The OM does not explain the gap. The 'Ready & tenanted' label also sits beside 7 vacant units, 2 expired leases counted as occupied and 2 let units with no Ejari. The headline return is therefore overstated and gives no net yield.
rejected_model_findings.analyst_action: Ask the broker to reconcile the OM's AED 3,310,000 to the unit-by-unit rent roll, and to say whether the 10.5% is gross or net and on what price. Recompute net yield from the rent roll and the operating statement, including the costs the statement omits (management fee, insurance, vacancy, sinking fund). Also confirm whether the 2025-26 statement is actuals or a projection.

memo.markdown:
## Verdict
**Needs work**: the deal is blocked because several hard mandate facts are unknown, and nothing else matters until they are resolved.

The blockers are:
- Asset type is not known.
- Title is not stated, and legal must check it before any further work.
- We don't know whether the location is in a mandate area.
- The minimum price test cannot be run because price is unknown.
- The maximum price test cannot be run for the same reason.
- Building age is not known.

I give no walk-away price and no buy recommendation.

## The deal
- **What and where:** The rent roll lists 84 units [[rr.unit_count]]: 56 studios [[rr.studio.units]], 24 1BR [[rr.1br.units]] and 4 retail [[rr.retail.units]]. Area, asset type, completion year and unit count could not be verified against the OM, so I did not use the OM's figures.
- **Price:** Asking price and price per sq ft are unknown. The OM states no price per sq ft.
- **Income:** In-place contract rent is AED 3.0m [[rr.in_place_rent_aed]]. At 31 October 2026 [[rr.as_of]], 92% [[rr.occupancy_by_units]] of units were let (91% [[rr.occupancy_by_area]] by area), with 7 vacant [[rr.vacant_units]]. The OM's lease structure failed verification, so lease terms rest on the rent roll alone. Studio rent averages AED 82 per sq ft [[rr.studio.avg_rent_psf]].

## Returns
The deal was not underwritten. Price, area and completion year are missing, so I give no returns and no walk-away price.

Mandate thresholds for later: unlevered IRR 7.5% [[mandate.target_unlevered_irr.threshold]], equity multiple 1.30x [[mandate.target_unlevered_equity_multiple.threshold]], going-in net yield on cost 6.0% [[mandate.min_going_in_net_yield_on_cost.threshold]]. Rent roll occupancy looks above the 90% [[mandate.min_occupancy.threshold]] minimum, but the mandate test is not formally run.

The OM headlines a 10% [[om.yield_stated]] yield and does not say what it is measured on or against. We can't compare it with a buyer's yield on price or cost until the OM states its basis.

The 12-month operating statement shows NOI of AED 2.4m [[opex.noi_aed]] before our adjustments. Expenses are 19% [[opex.opex_ratio]] of income, but the statement omits property management, insurance and a sinking fund. Real NOI will be lower.

## What would make it fail
- **Title or eligibility fails.** The mandate requires freehold single title and nothing supports it yet.
- **The headline yield does not hold.** The OM gives no basis for 10% [[om.yield_stated]], and the statement NOI leaves out standard costs.
- **Rent on weak leases.** AED 177,000 [[disc.expired_lease_counted_occupied.why]] of in-place rent sits on units with expired or unregistered leases.
- **Collection risk.** 30% [[notice.cheque_profile]] of rent is paid on six or more cheques, which means less post-dated cheque cover.

## Discrepancies
Listed most severe first. Lower-severity items are not discussed.

1. **Title not verified (high).** The OM's title statement could not be verified. The screen relied on nothing for title, and legal must confirm freehold status and any nationality restriction. This blocks the deal.
2. **Expired or unregistered leases shown as occupied (high).** Some units are marked occupied with leases that ended before the rent roll date, and other let units have no Ejari number. The screen relied on the rent roll's unit rows and rolled expired leases at the start of the analysis. About AED 177,000 [[disc.expired_lease_counted_occupied.why]] of in-place rent (5.9% [[disc.expired_lease_counted_occupied.why]]) sits on these units. An unregistered contract lacks legal standing, and a holdover tenant weakens the landlord's position.

## Checks before diligence
- Confirm asset type, area, asking price and completion year, and test them against the mandate.
- Obtain the title deed and DLD ownership records. Legal confirms freehold, single title and buyer eligibility.
- Request Ejari certificates and renewal status for the flagged units.
- Security deposits of AED 159k [[rr.deposits_aed]] transfer to the buyer and must be credited at closing.
- Review the cheque profile for collection risk.
- Get the OM's basis for its headline yield, and ask for the missing management, insurance and sinking fund costs.
- Standard first-pass items:
  - Ejari export reconciled to the rent roll unit by unit.
  - Building completion certificate.
  - Affection plan and permitted use.
  - Civil Defence and fire-safety certificates, and ACP cladding compliance.
  - Building condition survey and capex plan.
  - Retail leases: permitted use, trade licences and VAT treatment.

## Assumptions
Nothing was underwritten, so no exit yield, rent path, vacancy or leverage assumption drives a result. Any later walk-away price and returns will rest on the firm's house view (reference rent path, exit yield, vacancy and downtime), not on market evidence for this building. The package lacked asset type, title, area, price and completion year. Each stays unknown rather than defaulted, and each blocks the verdict.
